body:
This is a duplicate of:
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/109509

Leaving open but I don't think this is a bug but just an unusual unsupported case

> This is a duplicate of:
> 
> * [The function after @export_tool_button is having warning `The class variable "_tool_button_func" is declared but never used in the class.` #109509](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/109509)
> 
> Leaving open but I don't think this is a bug but just an unusual unsupported case

Personally, I think this case being unsupported *is* a bug. In what situation am I ever going to want a tool button callable to NOT be private? (The ability to just put `@export_tool_button` on a *function* would alleviate that issue, but with it needing to be on a variable of type callable, it's basically always just duplicate-referencing an existing function... so it would make sense to be private)

So, to be clear, this "unusual unsupported case" is 100% of cases I would ever use `@export_tool_button` for, which doesn't really seem "unusual".
I wouldn't say that's obvious, if it was why would the documentation not use a private variable?

> I wouldn't say that's obvious, if it was why would the documentation not use a private variable?

That's a good question, and I'd consider that a mistake in the docs. Unless you expect some **_other script_** to be **_changing which callable the tool button points to_**, it has no reason to NOT be private.

Can you give me any use case where a different script would be altering which callable a tool button calls? Because I think that would definitely qualify as the unusual case...

> The ability to just put `@export_tool_button` on a _function_ would alleviate that issue, but with it needing to be on a variable of type callable, it's basically always just duplicate-referencing an existing function...

Technically, exporting functions is impossible; the inspector only looks at the property list. Initially, we tried generating a fake property, but this presented a number of issues, both conceptual (the inability to change the property display order in the inspector without violating the recommended style guide, the inability to use dynamic tool buttons via `_get_property_list()`, and the need to rely on an implicitly generated fake property name in `_validate_property()`) and technical (changing the number of properties after the parse phase violated implicit assumptions of the analyzer and caused crashes due to invalid pointers after reallocating the member vector).

Strictly speaking, you don't need to create both a variable and a function to export a tool button. You can get by with just one variable. The most obvious way is to use a lambda:

```gdscript
@export_tool_button("Test")
var test_button: Callable = func () -> void:
    print("Test")
```

However, this has problems with `RefCounted` objects if the lambda explicitly or implicitly references `self`. You can use a getter to fix this:

```gdscript
@export_tool_button("Test")
var test_button: Callable:
    get: return func () -> void:
        print("Test")
```

Also, I have a [PR](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/99199) that could potentially shorten this syntax (note `=>` instead of `=`):

```gdscript
@export_tool_button("Test")
var test_button: Callable => func () -> void:
    print("Test")
```

Regarding the core of your issue (a false-positive warning about an unused private variable), I think we could add an exception for variables exported with `@export_tool_button`. However, this has one minor conceptual issue. GDScript doesn't have "true" private variables, they're just a naming convention. But if it did, you'd have to make **all** exported variables public, since they need to be accessible externally (via the Inspector and/or the serialization system). The only way private export variables work is because they aren't truly private.

From a practical standpoint, I agree with you: it makes sense to add an exception for `@export_tool_button` to the warning about unused private variables. But from a conceptual standpoint, this case confuses the concepts of public/private properties and internal properties (some languages ​​like C# have special attributes that hide identifiers from autocompletion and so on, but don't make them private).

> Strictly speaking, you don't need to create both a variable and a function to export a tool button. You can get by with just one variable. The most obvious way is to use a lambda:

Yes, but in most cases I've used this, I'm exposing an existing function that is used by other code as a button- so the need for the variable is the issue.

But yeah, shutting up the warning for tool buttons will help a lot.

> For now, how can we disable the linting rule?

```gdscript
@warning_ignore("unused_private_class_variable")
```
